selection_rationale: Twelve moving-coil dynamics and four ribbons that sound students meet on stages, in studios and in radio booths: the Shure SM58/SM57 and EV RE20/RE50 already used in TekPractice, Shure, Sennheiser, Beyerdynamic and AKG live and drum staples, and the Shure SM7B broadcast/podcast reference. The ribbon set covers a modern passive figure-8 (Royer R-121), a BBC-designed broadcast classic with a non-XLR connector and pin-1-positive wiring (Coles 4038), a large passive figure-8 whose maker also sells a phantom-powered sibling (AEA R84), and a hypercardioid double ribbon (Beyerdynamic M 160). The ribbons support the phantom-power lesson (rule R4) with each maker's own warning text.

devices.technology: Electrodynamic pressure gradient, passive figure-8 ribbon; 2.5-micron aluminum ribbon, rare earth neodymium magnets, offset-ribbon design (per Royer)
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: Royer says the R-121 helped put modern ribbon mics on the map in the 1990s. It is the go-to ribbon for electric guitar cabinets, and its max SPL is far higher than vintage ribbons.

key_specs.max_spl: >160 dB at 1 kHz; >135 dB at 20 Hz
key_specs.phantom_power: No power required. Royer manual: safe on phantom-powered consoles provided that the cabling is wired properly; do not patch through mic tie lines of a patch bay with phantom enabled (damaging phantom jolt); never test with an ohmmeter.

devices.notes: The manual also says the rear side should not exceed 115 dB SPL (front rated 135 dB) and that the preamp input impedance should be at least 1500 ohms (5x the mic impedance). R4 lesson: the risk comes from miswired cables and hot-patching through a patch bay with phantom on, not from correctly wired phantom alone.
